title: Man United Captain Fernandes Criticizes Carrick’s Tactics After Crushing Como Defeat – Al Jazeera
body:
Manchester United’s Europa League campaign suffered a further blow on Wednesday night when the Red Devils were outclassed 4‑1 by Serie A side Como in a shock first‑leg defeat. Mid‑fielder and club captain Bruno Fernandes did not mince words in the post‑match interview, lambasting the team’s lack of intensity and accusing manager Erik ten Hag of “playing a defeatist game” after an early concession set the tone for a night of missed opportunities and defensive frailties.

From the opening whistle, United appeared hesitant, allowing the visitors to settle into a rhythm that they would later exploit with ruthless efficiency. A swift early goal from Como’s forward forced United into a reactive posture, and according to Fernandes, the squad never managed to regain the proactive pressure that is a hallmark of the English side’s recent domestic success. “We gave away the ball too quickly, we didn’t press as a unit and we allowed them to dictate the game,” the Portuguese international said. “When you concede early, you have to respond with aggression, not with a mindset that we’re already behind.”

The tactical missteps went beyond a single lapse in concentration. Fernandes highlighted a lack of structural coherence, particularly in the midfield where United’s usual high‑pressing scheme gave way to a more passive, possession‑based approach that failed to disrupt Como’s build‑up. The midfield trio of Casemiro, Christian Eriksen and Fernandes himself appeared disconnected, with the latter admitting that the team “lost the shape” and allowed the opposition’s midfield to dominate the central zones. This loss of shape created space for Como’s wingers to exploit the flanks, resulting in two of their four goals coming from well‑timed crosses that caught United’s full‑backs out of position.

Defensively, United’s usual resilience was conspicuously absent. The back four struggled to communicate, leading to a series of individual errors that compounded the pressure. The third goal, a header from a corner, exposed a lack of organization in the box, while the fourth, a swift counter‑attack, highlighted the midfield’s inability to transition quickly from defense to attack. Fernandes, who often drops deeper to help shield the defence, expressed frustration at the “mental lapse” that seemed to pervade the squad. “We are a team that prides itself on fighting until the final whistle. Tonight, we seemed to accept defeat before the match even started,” he said.

The defeat also raises broader questions about United’s European ambitions under ten Hag. Since taking over, the Dutchman has emphasized a possession‑heavy, high‑pressing style that has yielded mixed results in the Premier League, but the European stage appears to demand a different level of tactical flexibility. Critics have argued that United’s reliance on a single pressing trigger leaves them vulnerable when opponents absorb pressure and force errors. The Como performance, with its disciplined defensive block and quick transitions, exposed this vulnerability in stark terms.

Looking ahead, United must regroup quickly if they are to salvage their Europa League hopes. The second leg, scheduled for next week in Manchester, offers a chance to overturn the deficit, but it will require a radical shift in approach. Fernandes hinted that the team will return to a more aggressive, high‑pressing template, with an emphasis on winning the ball higher up the pitch and preventing the opposition from establishing rhythm. Ten Hag is expected to make adjustments to the midfield composition, possibly re‑introducing players who can provide greater dynamism and pressing intensity.

The challenge now lies in translating that resolve into performance. United’s domestic form has been erratic, and the Europa League exit could become a catalyst for change or a further symptom of deeper issues. As the club looks to the upcoming fixtures, the pressure will mount on both the players and the coaching staff to demonstrate the fighting spirit that has long defined Manchester United’s identity. A decisive response in the return leg could restore confidence and keep their European campaign alive; a repeat of Wednesday’s lackluster display could see the season slipping further out of reach.
